title: 2. Yadunatha. The *Vallabha-digvijaya* (Sanskrit)
html:
The Sri Vallabha-digvijaya (also called the Yadunatha-digvijaya) is a Sanskrit prose life of Vallabhacharya composed by his grandson Yadunatha in Samvat 1667 [1610/11]; the text is a condensed list of events. Translated from the Sanskrit text of the 1985 edition (IA `vallabhadigvijayayadunathjimaharaj1985_202003_900_R`; the edition's Hindi translation and prefaces were not used); the 1908 edition kept in `sources/vallabha/` proved to be a different poem — Krishnashastri's Vallabha-digvijaya — and does not contain the meeting with Chaitanya (`CATALOG.md`). A tradition of the Vallabha school; in the lila database, category D.

2.1. The second journey to Jagadisha: the meeting with Krishna-Chaitanya (Purva-charitravachchheda; 1985 ed., p. 52 = PDF 88)

Charanadri (Chunar), Alarkapura (Adel), Vraja; Puri (Jagadisha), Gangasagara. Present: Vallabhacharya with his family and disciples; Krishna-Chaitanya.

1Then [the acharya] set out with his family on pilgrimage to Jagadisha.1 Having stayed at Varanasi and made the pilgrimage to Jagadisha, he returned to Varanasi.

2Then [the acharyas] with the family came to Charanadri.2 There took place a manifestation of Bhagavan's lila in Vyapi-vaikuntha. There, in Samvat 1572, in the year fifteen hundred and seventy-two, on [the day of] Mahalakshmi, Gosvami Sri Vitthalanatha appeared.3 At that time the Deity of Sri Vitthalanatha also came [to them]. A festival took place [as] in Nanda's house.

3Then they came to Alarkapura.4 There the samskaras of the children were performed. Then a fresh pilgrimage to Vraja was made. Then the great festival of Sri Gopinatha's sacred-thread ceremony took place. Then [the Deity] of Navanitapriya was brought through Garjana Dhavana.5 Then the acharyas with their disciples defeated and drove away Tandi-Vitandi.6 Then from Vadhujit … a gadya was obtained.7 At the annual festival the mother's command was carried out and Ekadashi was kept.

4Then, on the pilgrimage to Jagadisha — the arrival at Gangasagara. The meeting with Krishna-Chaitanya.8 The festival of the Ratha-yatra took place. Then there was the return from Jagadisha. Then — the pilgrimage to Haridvara.9

Notes

is the first of the three journeys of Vallabha to Puri named in this passage of Yadunatha; the third (p. 53) is to Gangasagara, where Vallabha received the command to complete the Subodhini (cf. § 1.4).

section 359, "kṛṣṇacaitanya-samāgamaḥ". In Yadunatha's chronology the meeting comes after 1516, at Puri, at the time of the Ratha-yatra, which agrees with the CC (Antya 7): Vallabha Bhatta came to the Lord at Puri, stayed there until the Lord humbled his pride in his learning, and was then received with mercy. Yadunatha gives no details. The meeting at Prayaga/Adaila (CC Madhya 19) is not mentioned by Yadunatha.

Notes

  1. "Jagadisha" (जगदीश, "Lord of the universe") — Jagannatha of Puri; "Jagadisha-yatra" — the pilgrimage to Puri. This
  2. Charanadri (चरणाद्रि) — Chunar on the Ganga near Varanasi, where, according to the Vallabha tradition,
  3. Samvat 1572 = 1515/16 CE. Vitthalanatha (Sri Gusainji), Vallabha's younger son, was born in 1516 (according to the
  4. Alarkapura (अलर्कपुर) — the Sanskrit name of Adel (Adaila) near Prayaga, where Vallabha lived (cf. § 1.5).
  5. Garjan Dhavan (in the vartas Gajan Dhavan) — a disciple of Vallabha; Navanitapriya — a Deity of the child Krishna,
  6. "तण्डिवितण्डि" — apparently the nickname of a sophist debater ("Tandi-vitandi", "empty wrangling and cavil").
  7. "अथ वधूजितो मातृजितां गद्यप्राप्तिरभूत्" — the passage is unclear: Vadhujit is apparently a name (cf. on the same
  8. "कृष्णचैतन्यमिलनम्" — Yadunatha's only mention of Chaitanya; in the table of contents of the 1985 edition this is
  9. The list then goes on to other events (Haridvara, the return to Alarkapura, etc.); Chaitanya is not mentioned
